newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures pare losses, seen in range.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures pare losses, seen in range.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures recovered most of their losses by Wednesday's close as players turned cautious about pushing the market lower ahead of a series of key events and economic indicators later in the week.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended 80 points lower at 18,255 after falling as low as 17,890 on concerns about Japan's banking sector following rumours, later denied, that Nippon Credit Bank was in financial difficulty.

Dealers said market participants were awaiting the outcome of the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting, which began on Tuesday, for confirmation that U.S. interest rates would be left unchanged for the time being.
The U.S. non-farm payrolls report for January on Friday and a weekend meeting of finance ministers from the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations are also expected to be focal points.
"There are a lot of events coming up so it's a little difficult to go entirely in one direction," said a senior Japanese bank dealer.
He said the market was likely to moved sideways on Thursday with support seen at 17,920 and resistance at 18,390.

Another trader said Nikkei cash and futures markets could be hurt if the dollar continued its bull run. The U.S. unit was quoted at 122.95/123.00 yen at 0815 GMT after hitting a four-year high of 123.18 yen in Tokyo earlier.
"People are waiting for the G7 and also to see whether this dollar is for real. If it rallies further, the Nikkei will get hurt," he said.
